comments.note: Null-value storage: JsonFileStorage::get() uses the ?? operator (as specified in WP). Storing null via set() then calling get() with a $default will return $default, making null indistinguishable from 'key not set'. This is spec-consistent but callers should avoid storing null intentionally.

Non-serializable values: If a PHP resource or circular-reference object is passed to set(), json_encode() returns false, and file_put_contents writes an empty string, silently corrupting the .json file. The mixed type hint on the interface makes this theoretically possible. Callers should restrict stored values to JSON-serializable types.

InMemoryStorage is not yet registered under autoload-dev in composer.json (noted by developer; deferred to WP-008). Any tests requiring InMemoryStorage before WP-008 must manually require the file or add a temporary autoload-dev entry.

summary: One blocking security issue found in JsonFileStorage::getFilePath(): path traversal vulnerability. $gridID is concatenated into the filesystem path without sanitization, allowing callers to escape the storage directory via sequences like ../. All other dimensions (maintainability, best practices, structure) are excellent. Requires one-line fix before PASS can be issued.

comments.note: BLOCKING — Path traversal in JsonFileStorage::getFilePath(). The method returns: $this->storagePath . '/' . $gridID . '.json' — with no sanitization of $gridID. A caller passing $gridID='../../config' or any path containing ../ can cause set() to write a .json file outside the intended storage directory and get() to read from it. This is OWASP A01/A03 (path traversal / injection). Fix: either (a) use basename($gridID) as a minimum safeguard, or (b) validate $gridID against a safe character pattern before use, e.g. matching /^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9\-_]*$/i (consistent with the existing column-name convention in constraints.md). Recommended approach is (b) — throw a DataGridException with a meaningful error code if the ID is unsafe, so developers catch the problem immediately rather than silently writing to an unexpected path.

Non-blocking: json_encode() can return false for non-serializable values (resources, circular references). In that case file_put_contents() receives false which PHP casts to an empty string, silently corrupting the .json file. The in-memory cache is updated so the caller sees no error within the same request; the data is lost on the next request. Already noted by QA as a spec-consistent edge case. Suggested follow-up: add a guard — if (json_encode(...) === false) throw a DataGridException — to make the failure explicit.

Non-blocking: file_put_contents() return value is not checked in set(). If the write fails (permissions, disk full, readonly filesystem), the cache is updated but the disk is not. The caller has no way to know persistence failed. A simple check — if (file_put_contents(...) === false) throw DataGridException — would surface this class of error promptly.

Single-character gridID (e.g., 'a') is accepted by the regex [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9\-_]* (the * allows zero trailing chars). This is correct per the pattern but may be surprising to callers who expect a minimum two-character ID. No AC requires a minimum length, so this is spec-consistent.

summary: Rework review PASS. All four review dimensions clear — the path traversal blocking issue from the previous code-review cycle has been fully resolved.

Security: validateGridID() is hoisted into getFilePath(), the single choke point for all path construction, providing complete protection for both get() and set(). Regex /^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9\-_]*$/ is appropriately strict.

Maintainability: code is clean and readable throughout. Per-request in-memory cache is a sound performance optimization. readGridData() defensive branches (missing file, false read, non-array decode) are all logically correct.
Best practices: LOCK_EX on file_put_contents prevents concurrent write corruption. JSON_PRETTY_PRINT appropriate for a local/LAN tool. No constructor property promotion (convention respected).
DataGridException::ERROR_INVALID_GRID_ID = 260300 follows YYMMNN format correctly (2026-03, seq 00).
InMemoryStorage: correct namespace, declare(strict_types=1), consistent null-storage behaviour matches JsonFileStorage by design.

Three low-priority non-blocking items remain deferred and acceptable: (1) json_encode() false-return guard in set(); (2) file_put_contents() return value check in set(); (3) mkdir() return value check in constructor. All are future-WP candidates.

comments.note: json_encode() can return false for non-JSON-serializable values (resources, circular references). In that case file_put_contents() receives false, which PHP casts to an empty string, silently corrupting the .json file. The in-memory cache masks the error within the same request. Suggested fix: add `if (($encoded = json_encode($data, JSON_PRETTY_PRINT)) === false) { throw new DataGridException('Cannot serialize grid data', null, DataGridException::ERROR_INVALID_GRID_ID); }` before the write.

file_put_contents() return value is not checked in set(). A disk-full or permissions failure silently returns false while the in-memory cache is updated, making the caller believe persistence succeeded. A simple `if (file_put_contents(...) === false) throw new DataGridException(...)` would surface this promptly.

mkdir() return value is not checked in the constructor. If directory creation fails silently, subsequent reads/writes will produce unexpected errors with no clear root cause. Adding a guard (check return or catch a potential error) would provide a cleaner diagnostic.
